title: Automated usage-policy mapping and restricted-weights flagging for model onboarding
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Problem: As the model catalog grows we get an increasing number of uploads with licenses and artifact bundles that are ambiguous with respect to allowed usage (commercial, redistribution, derivatives) and that sometimes include restricted or encumbered weights. Reviewer bandwidth is limited and manual triage introduces delays and inconsistent outcomes. We need a deterministic, auditable automation layer that maps on-upload license metadata and manifest indicators to Redwood-internal usage policy categories, computes a risk score, and surface a recommended disposition (auto-approve for serving, require manual review, place in holding state with escrow token, or block).

Scope: This ticket covers design and product acceptance criteria for the automation layer and the UI/console surfaces needed for reviewers and customers. Implementation work will be split across eng tickets (ENG-???), but this PRD defines mappings, score buckets, UI copy, and rollout constraints. The feature must integrate with existing model ingestion hooks and the provenance scanner (manifest signature checks). It must also publish a required flag for version pinning and performance profile publication gating: models above a risk threshold cannot be auto-published or have performance profiles visible externally until manual approval.

Outcomes: Reduce manual triage time by 60% for typical uploads, eliminate false-negative approvals for restricted-weights cases, and make onboarding decisions reversible with audit trail and reason codes.
acceptance_criteria: Automated license mapping produces one of: allowed-commercial, allowed-noncommercial, derivative-restricted, redistribution-restricted, unknown. Mapping rules documented in Confluence.

A risk_score (0-100) is computed using license mapping, presence of encumbered weight markers in manifest, model provenance confidence, and flagged dependencies; thresholds are configurable by policy.
Models with risk_score >= 75 are tagged 'holding' and blocked from public performance profile publication and auto-serving until an explicit manual approval is recorded.

Models with encumbered/restricted weights (manifest flag or checksum mismatch) are automatically flagged and assigned a temporary escrow token and queued for legal review; reviewers receive a single-click action (approve/reject/request-more-info).

Console shows an onboarding detail panel with: detected license(s), mapped policy category, risk score breakdown, recommended disposition, and links to evidence artifacts (MANIFEST, LICENSE, model card).
All automated decisions are logged with reason codes and stored in the audit log; an API endpoint exposes decision metadata for integrations.
Ability to override automation: reviewers can change the disposition and must provide a short reason; overrides increment a metric for human-review rate.
Unit and integration tests cover top 10 common license variants and at least 3 synthetic encumbered-weight scenarios.
Metrics dashboard (onboarding-safety) shows weekly counts for auto-approved, holding, manual-override, and blocked models.
Security review (KMS/HSM handling of escrow tokens and PII in manifests) completed before beta rollout.
implementation_notes:
High-level approach: add a License-to-Policy mapper service (stateless microservice) that accepts parsed license text and manifest metadata and returns policy category + rule hits. Combine mapper output with provenance scanner signals and a small weighted scoring function (weights configurable via remote feature flag). The onboarding pipeline should call mapper synchronously during ingest; decisions below auto-approve threshold will proceed to immediate publishing steps. Decisions above thresholds go to the ‘holding’ queue in the onboarding database and generate reviewer tasks.

Edge cases: multi-license bundles (apply most restrictive mapping), unknown or unparseable license -> conservative mapping (unknown -> derivative-restricted) with a note for manual review. For model forks where upstream license is unclear, surface chain-of-origin evidence and required manual attestation. For manifest checksum mismatch, mark as 'manifest-tampered' and escalate to security with highest priority.

Integration points: provenance scanner (ENG-6310), console onboarding panel (console-2025.11), audit-log service, and onboarding API. Feature flag gate required for risk thresholds and auto-approve toggle.

Data model: decision metadata includes decision_id, policy_category, risk_score, rule_hits (list of short codes), evidence_urls. Make these fields available via the onboarding API.

Performance: License mapping should complete within 300ms p95 at ingest to keep onboarding latency acceptable.
comments: 2026-03-10 Asha K: Initial PRD draft completed. Shared with Legal and Security for quick feedback. Added conservative default mapping for unparseable licenses.

2026-03-11 Marco R (Legal): Confirmed that GPL-family requires derivative-restricted mapping for downstream commercial serving; suggested adding explicit handling for AGPL. Updated mapping matrix in Confluence.
2026-03-12 Priya S (Security): Asked for threat model for manifest tampering and recommended escalation path to incident queue; flagged escrow token lifecycle as security-sensitive.
2026-03-13 Evelyn C: Pulled into the 2026-W10 cycle. Split eng work into separate tickets for mapper service, console UI, and API surface. Added performance and p95 SLA to implementation notes.
qa_plan: Create synthetic upload artifacts for 12 license variations (MIT, Apache-2.0, GPL-3.0, AGPL-3.0, CC-BY-4.0, proprietary, etc.) and assert expected policy mapping and recommended disposition.
Simulate manifest checksum mismatch and verify holding state, audit log entry, and reviewer task creation.
Verify that models above risk threshold do not have performance_profile.exposed == true and are omitted from public catalog search until approval.
E2E test: end-to-end upload -> mapper -> holding queue -> reviewer approve -> model transitions to published and performance profiles become visible.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal beta): Enable for 20% of uploads with feature flag and route decisions to reviewer queue but do not block publishing (monitor only). Phase 2 (limited enforcement): Block publishing for risk_score >= 90 and require manual approval; measure false-positives for 2 weeks. Phase 3 (enforcement): Full gating at configured thresholds, expose policy category in console and API. Provide bulk re-review tooling for backlog.
notes: This ticket focuses on the product surface and acceptance criteria. Engineering tasks will reference this ticket for implementation. Legal and Security have an open doc review—aim to incorporate feedback before Phase 2.
